destination.name: Orange
destination.tagline: A cool-climate Central West city at 862 m, known for apples, wine and autumn colour.
destination.description: Orange is a city of about 41,000 people in the Central West, 254 km west of Sydney at 862 m, and is named for Prince William of Orange rather than the fruit, which it is too cool to grow. Wikivoyage describes it as Australia's Colour City for its European trees, best seen in late March and April. Mount Canobolas, a long-extinct volcano that rises to 1,395 m, stands about 20 km to the west, and the surrounding wine region has been planted since 1980. The village of Carcoar, the third oldest settlement west of the Great Dividing Range, is a heritage stop in the district.
whyVisit: Walk the slopes of Mount Canobolas
Taste wine at Orange cellar doors
Wander the heritage village of Carcoar

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: Public transport runs only in town and to nearby district towns, so a car is the best way to reach Canobolas, cellar doors and Carcoar.

goodToKnow.title: Canobolas and snow
goodToKnow.detail: Mount Canobolas is closed when snow or ice is present, and Orange itself has severe frosts and some of mainland Australia’s few regular snowfalls outside the Snowy Mountains.

goodToKnow.title: Cellar-door hours
goodToKnow.detail: Cellar-door hours vary by winery, so check each one before you drive out.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are best, with the European trees in autumn colour in late March and April and mild days before the cold, frosty winters.
